included_when: the source states something concrete at the plant scene — an object, a rule, a promise, a capability or a relationship, not a mood
a later scene depends on it, such that removing the plant would change how that later scene reads
a reader could name both ends without being shown this file
excluded: ordinary continuity — a character still being where the last scene left them
facts the story asserts and never collects
pairs whose plant and payoff fall in the same scene
inclusion_rule.note: This records pairs a reader would name. It is NOT a claim about ADR 0020's trigger term, and it adds no pays_off edges to the package.

implicit.why: "she gave her a pair of glass slippers, the prettiest in the whole world" — the proclamation rests on the slipper being unique enough to identify one woman.
"she had excellent notions, and advised them always for the best" pays off when every lady at the ball wants her clothes and headdress copied.
The meanest work, the sorry garret and the straw bed are what the sisters beg pardon for at the end. Without the opening the forgiveness collects nothing.
She gives them the Prince's oranges and citrons; they then describe receiving them from a princess they cannot name. The irony gap is the payoff.
"lend my clothes to such a dirty Cinderwench" — refused, and Cinderella "was very glad of the refusal", then appears at the second ball dressed more magnificently than before.
The godmother appears unbidden at the fitting and makes her clothes richer than any before — the same agency, collected at the recognition.
The guards saw "nobody go out but a young girl, very meanly dressed". The fitting is that girl turning out to be the princess.
The sisters report he "was very much in love with the beautiful person who owned the glass slipper"; the proclamation is that resolve acted on.
"they did not know her" — held across seven scenes, and collected when they find her to be that fine, beautiful lady.
"The poor girl bore all patiently" is what makes the forgiveness in character rather than merely convenient, and it is why she lodges them in the palace.
The invitation's breadth is what lets an unknown princess be received without question.
